calculators.name: Rapid Prototyping - Parts per build
calculators.description: How many parts one build takes: the part's footprint on the plate, with the nesting allowance (nestingAllowance, 0.75 mm in memory/Rapid prototyping) on each side, laid in rows on the machine's bed, the better of the two ways round; a powder bed (SLS) also stacks them in height. Rapid Prototyping holds no base layers under the stack. Capped by the batch.

source.engine: build_height_mm (the part's height along the build direction)
stacks (1 for a laser sintered build, which needs no plate, else 0)

fields.name: Parts per Layer
fields.formula: max(floor({Bed Length} / ({Part Length} + 2 * {Nesting Allowance})) * floor({Bed Width} / ({Part Width} + 2 * {Nesting Allowance})), floor({Bed Length} / ({Part Width} + 2 * {Nesting Allowance})) * floor({Bed Width} / ({Part Length} + 2 * {Nesting Allowance})))

fields.name: Parts per Build
fields.formula: max(1, min({Batch Size}, {Parts per Layer} * {Parts Stacked}))

calculators.name: Rapid Prototyping - SLS powder
calculators.description: The powder one laser sintered part takes: the part itself, and its share of the bed's unfused powder that cannot be used again. The bed (its area times the stacked build's height) holds the powder at the material's density (memory/Rapid prototyping holds no tapped density); of what the parts do not fuse, the recoverable share (slsRecoveryPercentage) is used again and the rest is spent.

source.engine: bed_fill_height_mm (the stack of parts in the bed)

fields.name: Spent Powder Mass
fields.formula: max(0, {Bed Powder Mass} - {Parts per Build} * {Part Mass}) * (1 - {Recovery Fraction}) / max({Parts per Build}, 1)

calculators.name: Rapid Prototyping - Resin and support material
calculators.description: The material one printed or stereolithography part takes: the part at its density and price, and its supports. 3D printing prints them in a support material of its own (printingSupportMaterialDensity, printingSupportMaterialCost), solid: memory/Rapid prototyping holds no lattice spacing factor; stereolithography builds them of the part's resin, as solid as slaSupportVolumeFraction.

source.engine: support_fill (1 when printing, slaSupportVolumeFraction for stereolithography)
support_density (printingSupportMaterialDensity when printing, the resin's density for stereolithography)
support_unit_cost (printingSupportMaterialCost when printing, the resin's price for stereolithography)

calculators.name: Rapid Prototyping - Build gas
calculators.description: The nitrogen a laser sintering build consumes, at the machine's rate over the build's time, shared by its parts (the machine's nitrogen cost per litre; a machine that needs no external nitrogen pays nothing here).

fields.name: Gas Cost
fields.formula: {Nitrogen Rate} * {Build Time} / 3600 * {Nitrogen Cost} / max({Parts per Build}, 1)

calculators.name: Rapid Prototyping - Laser use
calculators.description: The laser a sintering or stereolithography build wears, at the machine's laser cost per hour (memory/Rapid prototyping Lookup laser_cost_per_hour for the sinterers, laser_replacement for the stereolithography machines) over the build's time, shared by its parts.

fields.name: Laser Cost
fields.formula: {Laser Cost per Hour} * {Build Time} / 3600 / max({Parts per Build}, 1)

calculators.name: Rapid Prototyping - Laser sintering
calculators.description: Laser sintering on a polymer powder bed (SLS), per part. The parts need no supports and are stacked in the bed: every layer at slsLayerThickness waits the machine's layer delay (the recoat), and each part is scanned at the machine's speed and beam. The build's preprocessing (slsPreprocessingTime) is shared by its parts. memory/Rapid prototyping holds no chamber heat-up or cool-down times, so none are charged.

source.engine: bed_fill_height_mm (the stack of parts in the bed)

fields.name: Cycle Time
fields.formula: ({Build Time} + {Preprocessing Time}) / {Parts per Build} * {Cycle Time Factor}

calculators.name: Rapid Prototyping - 3D printing
calculators.description: 3D printing (ProJet, Eden, V-Flash), per part. Each layer at the machine's layer thickness is printed by the head in strips along the bed: as many strips as the machine's scanning width takes to cover the nested parts' width, each crossed once at the machine's layer speed over the nested length (memory/Rapid prototyping holds no print head passes). The build's preprocessing (printingPreprocessingTime) is shared by its parts.

source.engine: nested_length_mm (the bed length the nested parts take)
nested_width_mm (the bed width the nested parts take)

fields.name: Cycle Time
fields.formula: ({Build Time} + {Preprocessing Time}) / {Parts per Build} * {Cycle Time Factor}

calculators.name: Rapid Prototyping - Stereolithography
calculators.description: Stereolithography (SLA), per part. Every layer at slaStandardLayerResolution is wiped across the bed (the bed length at the machine's wiper speed) and waits the machine's layer delay; each part and its supports (slaSupportVolumeFraction of the support volume) are cured by the laser at the machine's speed and beam. The build's preprocessing (slaPreprocessingTime) is shared by its parts.

fields.name: Scan Time
fields.formula: ({Part Volume} + {Support Volume} * {Support Fraction}) / ({Scanning Speed} * {Beam Diameter} * {Layer Thickness})

fields.name: Cycle Time
fields.formula: ({Build Time} + {Preprocessing Time}) / {Parts per Build} * {Cycle Time Factor}

calculators.name: Rapid Prototyping - Part curing
calculators.description: Post-curing in an oven (a stereolithography part in a ProCure or AaroCure oven, a LaserForm part in the LaserForm oven): one cure (curingMaxCureTime) per oven load, shared by the parts the oven's bed takes (Rapid Prototyping - Parts per build on the oven).

source.engine: parts_per_load (Rapid Prototyping - Parts per build, on the oven's bed)

fields.name: Cycle Time
fields.formula: {Cure Time} / max({Parts per Load}, 1) * {Cycle Time Factor}

calculators.name: Rapid Prototyping - Feature cleaning
calculators.description: The time to clear the loose powder or uncured resin from one hole or void (memory/Rapid prototyping cleaning* variables): its type's base time, times a multiplier of its size (a hole's diameter, a void's volume: below the Small limit the Small multiplier, above the Large limit the Large one, else the Medium one) and one of its depth (likewise). The engine seeds each input from the variable of the feature's type (simple, multi-step, ringed and complex holes; simple, ringed and complex voids).

source.engine: size (a hole's diameter in mm, a void's volume in mm³)

fields.name: Size Multiplier
fields.formula: {Size} < {Small Size Limit} ? {Small Size Multiplier} : ({Size} > {Large Size Limit} ? {Large Size Multiplier} : {Medium Size Multiplier})

fields.name: Depth Multiplier
fields.formula: {Depth} < {Small Depth Limit} ? {Small Depth Multiplier} : ({Depth} > {Large Depth Limit} ? {Large Depth Multiplier} : {Medium Depth Multiplier})

calculators.name: Rapid Prototyping - Cleaning
calculators.description: Cleaning the built part: the base time every part takes (cleaningBaseTime), plus the time of each of its holes and voids (Rapid Prototyping - Feature cleaning, summed by the engine over the holes and voids the cad-engine recognised).

source.engine: feature_time_s (every hole's and void's cleaning time)
